capabilities: Open .toml files in native Obsidian panes
Highlight TOML syntax with line numbers
Show parse errors as inline editor diagnostics and a validity status
extras: No screenshots or example TOML content; includes manual installation steps and a community plugin submission checklist referenced in a separate docs file.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to open or edit .toml files, so users must leave the app for an external editor.
summary: TOML file editor that opens .toml files in native Obsidian tabs with syntax highlighting, debounced autosave, and parse diagnostics.
